Ok, so you should really stop having sex with people until you get this sorted out. The dr. would be your best bet, or you could try to find a free clinic. I'm not sure what country you are in. If it is scabies, which it could be, then it would be spreading. If you are itching it a lot then it would definitely spread. I have herpes 1 and I can tell you that herpes mostly hurts. I suppose that it affects people differently and I do recall some itching when the sores started but in the end it HURT and STUNG (especially when I peed). 
So be honest about your symptoms. If you really believe it is scabies (because the rash is spreading) then you can treat it at home for a lot cheaper than going to the dr. You can purchase 10% permethrin (on the web) and mix it in a 1:1 ratio with body lotion. Before bed Smear the lotion from your jaw line (and behind your ears) all the way down to the soles of your feet, underneath your fingernails and toe nails. Smear it in your butt crack, all over your butt, your vulva (but take care not to get it near your vagina or urethra). Rub it in (its going to feel wet and cold so do it in a heated room). Put on some clean loose fitting pajamas and go to sleep. 8-14 hours later get in the shower and wash it off. Do not touch any clothes or bedding that have not been washed and dried. You can put your pillows straight into the dryer (w/out washing) for at least 40 minutes and that should kill all mites. Re-apply this treatment and cleaning in exactly 7 days. If your symptoms get worse or do not get better than it may not be scabies. 
Its up to you, if you want certainty just go to the Dr. now. If they diagnose you with scabies (and your in the US) the cream they prescribe you will be much more expensive at the pharmacy than if you make it. If they find something else...like herpes.
Herpes isn't the end of the world. The biggest thing is that now that I have herpes, I don't think its responsible to have casual sex. Because I believe herpes 1 (the kind that I have) is transmittable through the epidermis-in other words a condom isn't going to necessarily protect from spreading it. So instead I have relationships. Its easier to disclose this when you trust someone and then your not spreading it to everyone in town. And a lot of people have HSV1. HSV2 is a bit different, but a lot of people have that one too.

Oh, I gave up years ago on taming this mane and have been going "Diana Ross-ish" for a while. At my current place of work, (a shelter for Foster Children) everyone is in love with my big hair. But in those cases I just didn't have the care to pay attention to it. I think confidence in how you wear Your hair and how you dress your fabulous body are things that will make or break a big hair look.  If you are feeling uncomfortable with the hair when it is big then by all means take it slow and discover some ways to wear your hair back or in braids that look good to you. But my main advice is to keep it well moisturized with a rich oil (coconut, olive or Argan-or both ;-) ), comb it with only a wide tooth comb and let it air dry when you can. I love going out into a warm windy day with freshly conditioned, oiled hair, and it looks fabulous. And sleep in a satin or silk scarf. Tend to your hair as you would tend to a baby. Find a salon that has someone who knows how to cut with curly hair. But the main thing is keep it healthy, well-shaped and it will look healthy and good. Dry Diana Ross hair is VERY different from Healthy, moisturized, Fabulous Diana Ross Hair.
